newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine again delays T-bill payments.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine again delays T-bill payments.

text.p: Ukraine's finance ministry on Thursday delayed payment of interest and principal on Treasury bills for the third time in less than a month, bankers said on Thursday.

The finance ministry was due to repay 4.116 trillion karbovanets ($23.3 million) T-bill interest and principal due on September 18. The finance ministry usually effects payments the morning after the due date.
By late afternoon on Thursday, the money had still not been paid, bankers said.
Pravex Bank's chief of securities Alexander Tykhonyukh said his bank had no explanation why the money had not been paid.

"The central bank told us that the finance ministry did not send out the order to disburse the money, so they cannot send it," he said. Finance ministry officials, he said, were not answering their phones.
A finance ministry spokesman said he could not explain why the payments were delayed.
Ukraine has replaced the karbovanets currency with the hryvnia, but some calculations on T-bill transactions are still being conducted in the old currency.
The hryvnia, unchanged at 1.76 to the dollar since its introduction on September 2, equals 100,000 karbovanets.
On August 29, the ministry delayed a $23 million payment for half a day and on September 11 a similar delay occurred with a $22 million payment.
Yevhen Seltser of Bank Ukraina suggested the delays were caused by disagreements between the ministry and central bank.

"Earlier the bank gave the ministry short-term credits when it didn't have enough money to meet its payment obligations, but it looks like relations aren't great at this time and this practice has been discontinued," Seltser said.
Serhy Kryshevsky of TK-Kredit bank said the finance ministry had run out of money.
"It's obvious that the ministry is at a catastrophic level in terms of a money shortage and soon the payments will be delayed by two or three days," he said.
Kryshevsky added that few banks could risk taking the ministry to court for fear of repercussions later. --Natalya Zinets, Kiev Newsroom +380 44 229 2264
